children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to ask you some questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

Since Alex is 17, Child Benefit can continue beyond age 16 if the child stays in approved education or training (up until they turn 20).

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, doing A-levels, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He left school and isn't doing any courses right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**Is Alex currently working? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

This is relevant because if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either of these, you can still claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

Here's why:

Child Benefit is automatically available for children under 16. However, since Alex is 17, the rules are different. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can continue **only if** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex:
- Has left school
- Is not in any approved education or training
- Has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

He does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit.

**However, this could change if:**
- Alex returns to approved education or training (such as college, A-levels, or an approved training program)
- Alex registers with a careers service or the armed services (which would allow you to claim for up to 20 weeks)

If Alex's circumstances change in any of these ways, you would be able to make a claim for Child Benefit at that time.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and has left school. According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify if the child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Alex is not currently in approved education or training. Additionally, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, Alex has not registered with either of these services. Furthermore, the claimant would stop getting Child Benefit if the child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training - while Alex is not working, the key issue is that he is neither in approved education/training nor registered with a careers service or armed services. Therefore, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
